questions.q: In the Oracle Fusion supplier model, what does a 'supplier site' represent?
options: A person at the supplier's organization
The supplier's bank
A specific location or business arrangement with the supplier, carrying an address and operational controls
A purchase order
questions.explain: A site is a location/arrangement level record with an address, payment terms, tax details, and similar controls.

questions.q: What is required before a business unit can create transactions against a supplier site?
options: An active site assignment linking the site to that business unit
The supplier must have at least one contact
The supplier must be classified as a small business
The site must have a discount payment term
questions.explain: A site needs an active assignment to a business unit before that unit can transact against it, no matter how complete the site record is.

questions.q: What does an invoice attach to, rather than to the supplier directly?
options: A supplier contact
A business classification
A certifying agency
A supplier site
questions.explain: Invoices are entered against a site because the site carries the address, payment terms, and tax details that complete the invoice.

options: A duplicate supplier record awaiting merge
A person at the supplier's organization, such as someone who manages portal access or handles disputes
An alternate name for a supplier site
The GL account a supplier's invoices post to
questions.explain: A contact is a person, distinct from the address-level supplier site record.

questions.q: Vantree Industrial Parts has two sites, Columbus and Austin, both assigned to Brightfield's US business unit. What does the 'sold-to business unit' on each assignment represent?
options: The business unit that owns Vantree's bank account
The business unit where Vantree's contacts work
The business unit that approves Vantree's business classification
The business unit that assumes liability for purchases made through that site
questions.explain: The sold-to business unit, defined by the site assignment, is the organization that assumes liability for purchases against that site.
